text: There is nothing entered under your name. I looked twice. A paymaster's mate does not look a third time.
I may not open the strongbox just now. Orders. The Navy has regulations for the end of the world.
Entered. One per cent a round, the Navy's own rate. It is the only thing on this base that still pays on time.
Zahlstelle, Marinekasse Totenhafen. Thank God, a living face. Please speak quietly. The water carries.
Deposits, withdrawals, nothing else. The Commandant ordered the pay window kept open until relieved. Nobody has relieved me.
Your money, in full. Count it, please. I am not able to count just now.
The harbour master's ledger page. He left it in his hut on the quay, by the chart. Bring it to me and I can close the week, and pay out what is owed.
You put the Navy's cargo over the side. Three units. The manifest says ore. I have entered it as lost at sea, as ore. ...I did not enter who lost it.
That is the Kapitaenleutnant's key. He signed for her in this book. If she sails, I shall sign her out. It is the last thing in this port that can still be done properly.
They are on the apron again. I shall stay at the window. The window is my post.
Zahlmeistersmaat Jessen. The window is open, the books are kept. I was told to keep the pay window until relieved, and I keep what I am told.
The harbour master drew the last pay before he went down to the pens. He took the ledger page with him, and I cannot close the week without it.
The page. Thank you. ...There. The week is closed, the sums agree. What the harbour owes you, I can pay. Count it, please.
They are on the quay! On the quay! Shoot them, please, shoot them!
Gott im Himmel. I am only the paymaster's mate!
Somebody is down out there! Get them up, I cannot leave the strongbox!
